<STRUCT_0001>
The title of this section refers to the fact that we will use the
naive cotangent complex in this section. Let <MATH_0001>
be a deformation situation for a given category fibred in groupoids over a
locally Noetherian scheme <MATH_0002>. The key Example <REF_0001>
suggests that any obstruction theory should be closely related to
maps in <MATH_0003> with target the naive cotangent complex of <MATH_0004>.
Working this out we find a criterion for versality in
Lemma <REF_0002> which leads to a criterion for
openness of versality in Lemma <REF_0003>. We introduce a notion of
a naive obstruction theory in
Definition <REF_0004> to try to formalize
the notion a bit further.

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
In the following we will use the naive cotangent complex as
defined in Algebra, Section <REF_0005>.
In particular, if <MATH_0005> is a surjection of <MATH_0006>-algebras
with square zero kernel <MATH_0007>, then there are maps

whose composition is homotopy equivalent to zero (see
Algebra, Remark <REF_0006>).
This doesn't form a distinguished triangle in general as we are using
the naive cotangent complex and not the full one.
